newsitem.title: USA: Viacom to close New York CD-ROM office.
newsitem.headline: Viacom to close New York CD-ROM office.

text.p: Viacom Inc's Viacom New Media operations plans to close its New York office later this year and shift managment of its multimedia publishing business to its Virgin Interactive Entertainment division.
A spokeswoman for Viacom said the move will enable the company to reduce operating costs and reach profitability more quickly.
"We believe this will strengthen our position in the multimedia marketplace globally," the spokeswoman said.
About 70 people work at the New York office. Some of them may find jobs with in the Viacom divisions.
The move comes as the market for entertainment CD-ROMS has faced increased competition from other game-playing formats such as video game players and The Internet.
Viacom said its New Media label will publish the 1996/97 product slate, which will be distributed by Virgin.
Virgin is an operating unit of Viacom's Spelling Entertainment division.
Viacom New Media's Chicago development office will not be affected by the move.
The decision was first reported by Variety Wednesday.
